claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films are primarily governed by an interplay between nanostructure-induced magnetic-domain pinning and limited film–substrate heat transfer.
A 10–20 nm Cu interlayer can improve thermal coupling between the alloy film and substrate.
Improved film–substrate thermal coupling minimizes thermal lag during magnetic cycling.
Reducing thermal lag reduces magnetic-domain pinning.
Reduced magnetic-domain pinning narrows hysteresis and enhances the reversible magnetocaloric effect.
Magnetron sputtering can produce nanoscale HEA films on substrates.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or patterned nanoribbons can be produced by magnetron sputtering.
The proposed cycles use applied magnetic fields below 1 T near the alloy's magnetic phase-transition temperature.
Cycle frequency must remain within limits imposed by film–substrate heat transfer.
Grain boundaries and surface roughness in the nanostructured film modulate magnetic-domain dynamics and pinning.
Limited film–substrate heat transfer causes lagged temperature equilibration during magnetic-field cycling.
Lagged temperature equilibration exacerbates the effects of nanostructural defects and surface-induced domain pinning.
Thermal lag and domain pinning broaden hysteresis and reduce the magnetocaloric response.
Faster heat dissipation enables more complete and reversible magnetic phase transitions with less domain immobilization.
Relative to films without an interlayer, Cu-interlayer samples will exhibit a larger reversible temperature change.
Relative to films without an interlayer, Cu-interlayer samples will exhibit a narrower magnetic hysteresis loop.
The as-deposited baseline exhibits significant hysteresis and a muted magnetocaloric effect because of thermal lag and nanostructural domain pinning.
The magnetocaloric response is maximized near the alloy's intrinsic magnetic phase-transition temperature.
